seo.title: Costco: personalized recommendation carousels - $470M in sales in one quarter and 3x conversion (2026)
seo.meta_description: Costco personalizes costco.com and its app: carousels drove over $470M in sales in Q2, converted three times better, and 10% of orders included a personalized item.
seo.resume_citable: Costco's personalized product recommendation carousels on costco.com and in its app generated more than $470 million in e-commerce sales in the second quarter of fiscal 2026 and converted three times better than the site's usual rate in the third; in the fourth quarter, 10% of costco.com orders contained a personalized item, according to CFO Gary Millerchip on the earnings calls.

faq.a: Personalized product recommendation carousels on costco.com and in the app, based on the member's history, notably past searches. In Q4 of fiscal 2026, personalization extends to product placements and emails.

More than $470 million in e-commerce sales generated by the carousels in Q2 of fiscal 2026, conversion three times the usual rate in Q3, then in Q4 triple-digit growth in sales from personalization and 10% of costco.com orders containing a personalized item.

faq.q: Is traffic from AI search part of this result?
faq.a: No. Traffic from external AI search engines, growing at triple digits according to Costco, comes from third-party assistants. It is an acquisition channel separate from on-site personalization.

pattern: personalized product recommendation carousels based on member history, on the site and the app
objectif_business: Close the digital gap of a retailer whose e-commerce accounts for a small share of revenue, by making the site and the app more relevant to each member: more items in the online basket, more visits, and a stronger member relationship at a time when memberships taken online renew slightly less well than those taken in the warehouse.
description: Costco began personalizing its site and app in the first quarter of its fiscal 2026 (September to November 2025). CEO Ron Vachris then presented new capabilities that offer members more relevant product recommendations based on their search history. The most visible format is the personalized product recommendation carousel, placed on costco.com and in the app. CFO Gary Millerchip reports its results quarter after quarter on the earnings calls. In the second quarter (call of March 5, 2026), the carousels generate more than $470 million in e-commerce sales. In the third quarter (call of May 28, 2026), they convert three times better than the site's usual conversion rate; Retail Dive reports that Millerchip puts their contribution at just under $500 million in digital sales, while the Motley Fool transcript of that passage carries an obvious amount error. In the fourth quarter (call of September 24, 2026), Costco widens the scope to product placements and emails: sales from personalization initiatives show triple-digit growth and 10% of costco.com orders contain a personalized item. Costco discloses neither the model, nor the vendor, nor the method used to measure these attributed sales, and does not itself call the carousels AI on its calls; it is the retail press (Retail Customer Experience) that describes them as AI-powered. Not to be confused with a result of this system: traffic from external AI search engines, which Costco says is growing at triple digits on the same call, comes from third-party assistants and not from Costco's personalization.
points_cles: Since late 2025, Costco has served personalized recommendation carousels on costco.com and in its app.
Suggestions draw on the member's history, notably past searches, according to CEO Ron Vachris.
More than $470M in sales via the carousels in Q2 of fiscal 2026, 3x conversion in Q3.
In Q4, 10% of costco.com orders contain a personalized item, figures given on an earnings call.

resultats.metrique: E-commerce sales generated by the personalized recommendation carousels, Q2 of fiscal 2026
Carousel conversion rate compared with the site's usual conversion rate, Q3 of fiscal 2026
Share of costco.com orders containing a personalized item, end of fiscal 2026
Growth in sales from personalization initiatives (product placements and emails included), Q4 of fiscal 2026

niveau_preuve.justification: The figures are stated by Costco's CFO in his prepared remarks on three consecutive earnings calls (Q2, Q3 and Q4 of fiscal 2026), cited here through the transcripts published by The Motley Fool, and picked up by Retail Dive and Digital Commerce 360. Earnings communication, several consistent sources; the AI label for the engine comes from the trade press, not from Costco.

stack_technique.detail: Deployed on costco.com and the app. Costco discloses neither the model nor the vendor of the engine.

fonctionnement_operationnel.cadence: Continuous: the carousels recompute as the member browses. Steering happens quarterly, with Costco reporting attributed sales and conversion on each earnings call.
fonctionnement_operationnel.opere_par: Costco's e-commerce and digital teams; no vendor is named in the sources.
fonctionnement_operationnel.signal_pilote: The logged-in member's history, in particular past searches. An unidentified visitor or a member with no online history gives almost nothing to work with, which limits the reach of the carousels for members who mostly buy in the warehouse.

etapes.detail: The site and the app record the member's searches and purchases, tied to their membership number.
The engine selects the products to push in the carousels based on this history.
The personalized carousels appear on costco.com and in the app; in Q4, the same logic feeds product placements and emails.
Costco tracks sales made through the carousels, their conversion against the site's usual rate and the share of orders containing a personalized item, then reports them to investors.

prerequis_data: customer identified at login, ideally by an account or membership number shared by the store and the site
usable online search and purchase history per profile
tracking able to attribute a sale to a carousel and compare its conversion with the site rate
prerequis_orga: an e-commerce team that owns the carousel slots on the site and the app
a sales attribution rule set before launch, so that the reported figure is defensible
a merchandising decision on what the engine is allowed to push
stack_possible: in-house recommendation engine or e-commerce personalization platform
CDP or customer data warehouse linked to the account
email tool able to reuse the same recommendations
replication.premiere_etape: Place a first personalized carousel on a high-traffic page for logged-in customers, and measure its conversion against the site's usual rate before extending to other slots.

playbook.action: Tie online searches and purchases to a single customer identifier, and measure what share of traffic is logged in.
playbook.livrable: Usable customer profile and size of the addressable audience.

playbook.action: Launch a recommendation carousel on a priority slot, with a control group receiving no personalization.
playbook.livrable: Carousel conversion read against the usual rate and against the control group.

playbook.action: Extend to the other slots on the site and the app, then reuse the recommendations in emails and product placements.
Track attributed sales, conversion and the share of orders containing a recommended item at each reporting cycle.
playbook.livrable: Personalization dashboard reviewed by senior management.

replication.equipe: An e-commerce product manager who owns the slots, data science profiles for the engine and attribution, front-end developers for the site and the app, with merchandising as a guardrail on the assortment being pushed.

statut_vivant.note: The system is cited on four consecutive calls, from Q1 to Q4 of fiscal 2026, and its scope widens in Q4 (product placements, emails). The Q3 amount is known only through the press: the Motley Fool transcript of that call shows a figure in billions that is inconsistent with the other sources.

transposable_ue.note: The recommendations rely on search and purchase history tied to the member account. In the EU, this marketing profiling requires a legal basis and, for trackers on the site and the app, GDPR and ePrivacy consent. A product recommendation engine is not high risk under the AI Act. The membership club model, where every customer is identified, makes data reconciliation easier but does not remove the obligation to inform members.
